articles.title: Elke Sommer, prolific German star of A Shot in the Dark and And Then There Were None, dies aged 85
articles.summary: The Berlin-born performer had a gift for languages that took her to Hollywood, landing roles alongside Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman. Elke Sommer, the prolific German star of the Pink Panther film A Shot in the Dark, early 70s Agatha Christie adaptation And Then there Were None, and…
body: German-born Sommer, whose best-known film roles were in the 1960s and 70s, was one of the wave of European performers who crossed over to Hollywood and English-language cinema with considerable success, following the postwar emergence of European new wave cinema. Sommer was one of the few German actors to make waves at the time, as Hollywood made much of her bombshell image.

Born Elke Schletz in 1940 in Berlin, the daughter of a Protestant pastor, she was evacuated with her family to Bavaria during the war. Intending to work as an interpreter, she was spotted by celebrated Italian director Vittorio De Sica after winning a beauty contest on a trip to Italy in 1958, and subsequently offered roles in a string of Italian comedy films. She crossed back into more serious work with the West German drama The Death Ship, opposite Horst Buchholz (who would go on to appear in cowboy classic The Magnificent Seven).
points: The Berlin-born performer had a gift for languages that took her to Hollywood, landing roles alongside Peter Sellers, Dick Van Dyke and Paul Newman.

In addition to starring, Glover and his brother and frequent collaborator Stephen Glover will write and executive produce the “PUBG” show…
body: “PUBG” was originally published by Krafton in 2017. The game does not have a plot, but rather sees large numbers of players dropped into one of several maps featuring a wide array of weapons, vehicles, and other items in a last-man standing deathmatch. Exact plot details for the potential show are under wraps.

“PUBG” is one of the most popular video games in the world even nearly 10 years after it was released. It broke multiple Guiness world records upon its initial release and continues to pull in hundreds of thousands of active users daily.

Donald and Stephen most famously worked together on the hit FX series “Atlanta.” Donald created and starred in the show, with Stephen serving as a writer and executive producer throughout its four-season run. They then teamed on the Amazon series “Swarm” and the musical film “Guava Island,” with Stephen also writing for Donald’s Amazon series “Mr. and Mrs. Smith.”

Donald is also known for his work on shows like “Community” and “30 Rock,” as well as for starring in films like “The Martian,” “Spider-Man Homecoming,” “Solo: A Star Wars Story,” and “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.”

articles.title: Cannes Chief Thierry Fremaux Hails French Film Model as CNC Head Gaëtan Bruel Vows to Fight for Its Future at 80th Anniversary
articles.summary: France’s National Film Board, the CNC, marked its 80th anniversary with a three-day gathering of industry leaders in Paris, including Cannes Film Festival chief Thierry Frémaux who praised the country’s unique film funding system.
body: Bruel warned against attempts to dismantle a model that has helped make France a global cinema powerhouse.
Frémaux, who also heads the Institut Lumière in Lyon, highlighted the CNC’s key role on display across films showcased at Cannes and other major festivals.

“We don’t say it because the Americans accuse us of constantly favoring certain things, because they themselves cannot imagine that the selection process is conducted in complete independence. But you can see just how much French money, the CNC and French professionals are absolutely everywhere,” Frémaux said during an onstage conversation with film historian Antoine de Baecque at the French Cinémathèque on Wednesday.
Frémaux also pointed out the CNC’s support for film restoration, noting that countries around the world have begun developing similar initiatives.

articles.title: Andrew Tate Docuseries ‘Toxic Empire’ Set at Investigation Discovery
articles.summary: Investigation Discovery (ID) will release a new four-part docuseries on the infamous brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate, Variety has learned. Titled “Andrew Tate: Toxic Empire,” the four-part series will have its two-hour premiere on Nov. 25 on ID at 9pm ET/PT.
body: “As Andrew Tate built a global following of millions with content promoting wealth, health, male dominance and misogyny, his rise drew both devoted fans and mounting allegations. The docuseries offers a comprehensive look at the story that has dominated headlines, featuring unprecedented access to male followers, insiders, alleged survivors, investigative journalists and extensive Tate archive, to explore how the lines between aspiration and exploitation became blurred.”

The docuseries will explore how the brothers recruited male followers and launched their webcam business and what they referred to as their “PhD” (Pimping Hoes Degree) course, which allegedly taught men coercive methods to recruit women into webcamming while retaining most of the profit for themselves. It will also feature interviews with former followers and associates.
The series is directed and produced by Julian P. Hobbs, Elli Hakami and Adrian Murray for Investigation Discovery.

articles.title: I Love Boosters review – supercool outlaw women go shoplifting in Boots Riley’s frantic and funny caper
articles.summary: Demi Moore’s haute-couture maven attracts the attention of a gang of contemporary Robin Hood type clothes robbers in Riley’s fashion biz satire. Here is an entertaining, if very exhausting fantasy-caper about the fashion biz from Boots Riley, a madcap mile-a-minute melee of unadulterated…
body: She plays Christie Smith, a billionaire couture designer who has an office in a trendily designed city block which leans over at an experimental angle. Christie is the object of obsessive attention from “boosters”: supercool young outlaw women who, nettled by her arrogance, shoplift her clothes from upscale stores and sell them on at knockdown Robin Hood prices. They are Corvette (Keke Palmer), Sade (Naomi Ackie) and Mariah (Taylour Paige), the latter having the ability to, by holding her breath, turning herself into a white woman who is less likely to be challenged in a store; an interesting metaphor for what Frantz Fanon might have called black skin, white masks.

For all their savvy, the boosters have a soft spot for certain men in their lives, notably a charismatic community leader called Dr Jack (Don Cheadle), who is running a friendship self-help scheme that is actually a fraudulent pyramid scam. And Corvette is entranced by a laidback charmer and oral sex enthusiast played by LaKeith Stansfield, who turns out to be a demonic male succubus.

articles.title: Exploding heads, mutant aliens and bursting chests: horror’s greatest special effects – ranked!
articles.summary: From the beheading in The Omen to the attic scene in The Birds, here’s a countdown of the genre’s most iconic moments – in glorious, old-school pre-CGI style. Towards the end of the 20th century, when film-makers’ overreliance on CGI was increasingly making special effects less special, it took the…
body: The Swedish director Victor Sjöström makes extensive use of double exposure – all done in-camera because optical printing had yet to be developed – to depict Death’s soul-collecting carriage in this folk-horror classic. Sjöström also plays the dissolute antihero, condemned to be the spectral vehicle’s driver unless he can mend his ways.

Henrik Galeen’s expressionist variation on the Faust legend reunites the stars of The Cabinet of Dr Caligari: Conrad Veidt plays the student who makes a deal with the devil (Werner Krauss), who steals his reflection. This evil doppelganger runs amok until Veidt confronts it in a split-screen climax.

FW Murnau commandeers a variety of in-camera effects for this vampire masterpiece. Flipped negatives, sped-up action and stop-motion add to the unheimlich ambience until, exposed to the sun’s rays, cadaverous Count Orlok (Max Schreck) vanishes in a puff of smoke.

Raise a glass to Jim Krut, who died in August but who will forever be remembered as “Helicopter Zombie” in George A Romero’s undead classic. Thanks to the magic of splatter makeup maestro Tom Savini, he shambles into frame – and gets the top of his head sliced off by a spinning rotor.

articles.title: Wicker review – Olivia Colman finds the perfect lover in intriguing folk-horror romance
articles.summary: Colman stars as a depressed and bullied fisherwoman in medieval England. Fortunately, Peter Dinklage’s basketmaker delivers the answer to her dreams – an Alexander Skarsgård made of wicker.
body: The spirit of mystery author Shirley Jackson is interestingly revived in this peculiar folk-horror romance, adapted from a 2006 story called The Wicker Husband by British writer Ursula Wills. It’s almost funny but not exactly, and almost disturbing but not exactly, occupying a strange and intriguing Venn-diagram overlap between macabre horror and sentimentality. Yet devotees of bucolic British screen-scariness will note that it is, after all, about a wicker man.

The scene is a fabular medieval-effect village that could be in central Europe or England, where there are bizarre patriarchal rituals, like the placing of metal collars on new brides. A depressed middle-aged fisherwoman (fiercely and naturalistically played by Olivia Colman) lives alone in a remote cottage and regularly brings her unappetising tench and gudgeon to market, where she is mocked and bullied by the nasty, closed-minded locals, including Richard E Grant as a lazy and incompetent doctor. Chief among her tormentors is the spiteful tailor’s wife, an elegant, sharp-faced woman played by Elizabeth Debicki.

Fortunately, Peter Dinklage’s basketmaker delivers the answer to her dreams – an Alexander Skarsgård made of wicker.

articles.title: George Michael's Faith guitar sells for £180k after auction row
articles.summary: The brother of the singer's late personal assistant said she would not have wanted the items to be sold.
body: The guitar George Michael performed with in his 1987 Faith music video has sold for £180,000 at auction, after a row over the sale of memorabilia related to the singer.

The guitar was one of more than 30 items auctioned by Sworders from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, Michael's long-time personal assistant. The sale fetched a total of £238,000 excluding buyers' premium.
Bailey died in 2014 and the items were sold by her estranged husband Ian Belcher, who inherited them after her death.

Gerard Bailey, Siobhan's brother, told the BBC she "would be horrified at the prospect of the auction being held in her name and that her personal, cherished possessions are being sold off to the highest bidder". Sworders and Belcher declined to comment.
points: The brother of the singer's late personal assistant said she would not have wanted the items to be sold.

articles.summary: He got famous playing video games but now you're more likely to see Seán McLoughlin in one.
body: He started uploading in 2012, in what many people consider to be the platform's "golden age" when vlogging, video game playthroughs and comedy escapism were all the rage.
Like many in the content creation space, he's been branching out in recent years, taking more acting jobs and getting involved in film production.

articles.title: Investigation Discovery to Probe Andrew Tate Allegations in ‘Toxic Empire’ Docuseries
articles.summary: The four-part series will chart the controversial social media personality's rise as he sits in a U.S. jail, along with brother Tristan, fighting extradition to the U.K. on rape and sex trafficking charges.
body: The controversial rise of Andrew Tate, a promoter of toxic masculinity across social media platforms, will be the subject of an upcoming Investigation Discovery docuseries.

The four-parter, Andrew Tate: Toxic Empire, is set to debut Nov. 25 on ID and follows Tate and his brother, Tristan, in July 2026 being arrested and jailed in Miami as British authorities seek their extradition on rape and sex trafficking charges.

Andrew and Tristan Tate are former kickboxers who built a large online following by sharing extreme masculine and misogynistic content. Andrew Tate first rose to prominence on the U.K. reality show Big Brother in 2016, only to be removed after just six days in the house after footage surfaced appearing to show him attacking a woman.

The brothers, who were born in the United States and moved to the United Kingdom as children, hold dual citizenship. They are under criminal investigations in Britain and Romania. The Tate brothers were charged with 21 crimes in the U.K., including rape, actual bodily harm and human trafficking.
